additions.site_name: DataBank DEN4 Westminster Data Center (7579 W. 103rd Avenue)
additions.name: DataBank DEN4 — existing edge colocation data-centre operations

status.summary: DataBank's Westminster Data Center page, in its version modified on 28 September 2026 (bounded below by the Internet Archive copy of 12 July 2026, modified 14 May 2026, with identical facility text), names '(DEN4)' at 7579 W. 103rd Avenue, Westminster, CO 80021 and describes it as 'a premier edge colo facility and one of the few data centers in the Denver north metro area' whose 'carrier-neutral interconnection hub provides cross connect options to on-site carriers, ISPs and fiber networks', with 9,890 IT square feet, 0.5 MW critical IT load, 3 onsite carriers, cabinets and cages colocation, a 100% uptime SLA, staffed hours and remote hands; DataBank's Denver market page (version of 27 September 2026, already held as Atlas evidence for DEN1 and DEN3) lists DEN4 among its five Denver data centers. This records existing operation on 28 September 2026, the modification day of the captured version; it is not an opening date. The square footage and 0.5 MW are stated ratings, not load in service.

locator.precision: Centroid of Jefferson County parcel 29-141-01-015 from the State of Colorado public parcel composite (county data received 21 April 2026; situs 7579 W 103RD AVE, land use 'Data Centers', 2.29 assessor acres, 2.26 geodesic acres, about 143 by 81 m). It locates the parcel holding DataBank's DEN4 address, not the building footprint or a surveyed position.
locator.identity_review: DataBank gives DEN4's address as 7579 W. 103rd Avenue, Westminster, CO 80021 on its facility and Denver market pages. The state parcel composite returns one parcel at that situs, Jefferson County 29-141-01-015, owner of record ZCOLO LLC with county land use 'Data Centers' (the zColo data-center assets were acquired by DataBank from Zayo in 2020, per DataBank's 15 December 2020 release; the release does not name this facility, so no owner role is asserted), and the statewide address point for 7579 W 103RD AVE lies inside the parcel 6.9 m from the centroid. No geocoder, map viewport or city centroid is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The state composite publishes no positional accuracy for county parcel polygons; the centroid represents a 2.26-acre parcel (furthest vertex 82.6 m from the centroid) whose building footprint is not separately located.

additions.site_name: Meta Los Lunas Data Center (4250 Messenger Loop NW, Huning Ranch Business Park)
additions.name: Meta Los Lunas Data Center — existing data-centre operations

status.summary: Meta's Los Lunas Data Center fact sheet, dated 2 September 2026 and published through Meta's Los Lunas asset link by 3 September 2026 (the link still resolved to the January 2025 version on 10 August 2026), says the Los Lunas Data Center is part of Meta's global infrastructure, gives '400+ Operational jobs supported', states that 'Our operational data center buildings achieve LEED® Gold certification' and that 'Since our Los Lunas Data Center went online in 2018' Meta has supported local organizations, with USD 2.5B+ investment and ground broken in 2016. This records existing operation of the Los Lunas Data Center on 2 September 2026, the date of the revised fact sheet; it is not an opening date, and it does not establish that every building of the 2021 two-building expansion is complete.

locator.precision: Centroid of Valencia County parcel UPC 1006040520058000000 (Huning Ranch Business Park Tract A4A, 4250 Messenger Loop NW; 284.99 recorded acres, 285.04 geodesic acres, about 1,307 by 970 m). It locates the tract that holds the campus's data-hall buildings, not an individual building; support buildings and a second substation lie on the adjoining Tract A3A and a substation on Tract A4B.
locator.identity_review: Meta names its Los Lunas Data Center in Valencia County, New Mexico. The Village of Los Lunas's notice for the 2026 Meta Los Lunas Data Center Community Action Grant Ceremony states that the event 'will take place at the Meta Los Lunas Data Center located at 4250 Messenger Loop NW, Los Lunas, NM 87031', and the Village's economic-development page names the 'Los Lunas Meta (Facebook) Data Center campus' among its largest employers. Valencia County's address point for 4250 MESSENGER LOOP NW carries UPC 1006040520058000000 and lies inside this parcel (situs 4250 MESSENGER LOOP NW; owner of record Village of Los Lunas, fully exempt). The adjoining Tract A3A of the same plat is owned by Greater Kudu LLC with owner address 1 Hacker Way, Menlo Park, and the county's 2024 orthoimagery shows the rows of large data-hall buildings inside Tract A4A. No geocoder, map viewport or village centroid is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The county publishes no positional accuracy for its parcel polygons (stored in NAD83 State Plane and returned in WGS84 by the county server); the centroid represents a 285-acre tract (furthest vertex 819 m from the centroid) whose buildings are not separately located.

additions.site_name: Site Layer 1 Data Center Project (near Playas, Grant County, New Mexico)
additions.name: Site Layer 1 Data Center Project — proposed data centre of about 800 MW with 300 MW on-site gas-engine generation

status.summary: Site Layer 1, LLC's initial NSR air-quality construction permit application to the New Mexico Environment Department, under a cover letter of 7 October 2026 and listed by NMED as the 'Initial Construction Permit Application' for 'Site Layer I, LLC – Site Layer I data center' (Grant County), is titled 'Site Layer 1 Data Center Project' and states that 'Site Layer 1, LLC (Site Layer 1) is proposing to construct a data center powered by a natural gas–fired electrical power generation development (the “Project”), on private land in Hidalgo and Grant Counties, New Mexico', with an anticipated data-center size of approximately 800 MW and about 300 MW of on-site generation from 32 Wärtsilä 20V34SG gas engines. The facility is 'Not Constructed'; construction is targeted for Q1 2027 to Q3 2028 and start-up for Q4 2028. This records the project as announced on 7 October 2026. The permit is pending, so neither consent nor works are asserted; the 800 MW and 300 MW figures and the dates are applicant targets.

locator.precision: Facility location given in Section 1-D of the application (latitude 31.980569, longitude -108.511384, NAD 83; UTM zone 12 735,145 E, 3,540,987 N; Grant County; 4.9 miles north-east of Playas). It marks the proposed gas-engine power plant of the Project, 44.7 m north of the midpoint of the modeled 32-engine stack row; the preliminary layout draws the four data-centre buildings beside the engine hall but gives them no coordinates. It is not a surveyed building, parcel or boundary, and the wider Project extends across 7,214.4 acres of generation project area and into Hidalgo County.
locator.identity_review: The application's cover letter, title page, Application Summary, modeling report and Figure 2 ('Data Center & Gas Engine Site Plan') all identify the Site Layer 1 Data Center Project of Site Layer 1, LLC and place the permitted facility at this coordinate; the Section 1-D decimal degrees agree with the stated UTM coordinates to 0.7 m, and the 27 August 2026 public-notice letters give a point 45.2 m away at the engine row. NMED's public-notices page lists the same application for 'Site Layer I, LLC – Site Layer I data center' under Grant County. The layout sheet's title block carries another project's name and a coordinate 18.6 km to the south-east; the form, letters and modeled stacks agree on the selected point, so the title block is treated as a drafting carry-over and not used. No geocoder or map viewport is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The applicant states the coordinate to six decimal places and UTM values to the nearest 10 m without a survey accuracy; it locates the planned engine plant, while the planned data-centre buildings sit beside it at undisclosed positions on a much larger private project area.

additions.name: Apple Prineville Data Center Campus — eastern campus expansion (PRZ 06 development area)
additions.site_identity_review: The City of Prineville's Resolution 1654 packet identifies the expansion as the 'eastern portion' of Apple's own Prineville data-centre campus, the 'PRZ 06 development area', and its development agreement describes that campus as the real property within the City on which Apple owns and operates a data center campus (recital A, Exhibit A). This is the same campus, the same agreement and the same City record that establish the existing Atlas site curated:apple-prineville-data-center-campus (vcc-site-9bb771ea13115bdd8091; project 'Apple Prineville Data Center Campus — existing operations', whose status evidence is this packet). Exhibit A labels the APPLE CAMPUS (and the Exhibit B pipeline map hatches it east of Prineville Airport) and shows the PRZ06 offsite lines reaching its north side and running along its eastern edge. The expansion is therefore a further phase of the existing campus, not a separate physical site; its buildings are not yet described.

status.summary: The City of Prineville's packet for its 13 October 2026 council meeting (generated 8 October) presents Resolution 1654 and a development agreement under which the City procures and oversees the 'PRZ-06 Offsite Utility Expansion Project', 'utility improvements necessary to serve Apple's eastern campus expansion'. The staff report states that 'Apple's initial development plan included the expansion of the easter[n] portion of its campus', which requires these offsite water, non-potable water, sanitary sewer and industrial-wastewater lines, and recital B of the agreement describes the project as the infrastructure 'needed to serve the eastern portion the User's campus PRZ 06 development area'. The council adopted the resolution unanimously on 13 October 2026. This dated government record announces Apple's planned eastern campus expansion in the PRZ 06 development area of its existing Prineville data-centre campus. It does not describe the expansion's buildings, floor area, power or IT capacity, and no land-use approval, building permit or site work for the expansion is asserted; the utility contract's 31 March 2028 Final Completion target and the 350 gpm future water reservation (until 30 September 2028) are forecasts and reservations, not observations, and the offsite utility works themselves are not treated as a construction stage of the data-centre expansion.

locator.identity_review: Reuses the existing Apple Prineville Data Center Campus locator exactly: the centroid (-120.8659538, 44.2845822) of the union of the three Crook County tax lots owned by Apple Inc (1515000000312 at 1600 SW Baldwin Rd, 1516070000101 and 1516070000102; one contiguous 364-acre holding), with its pinned geometry evidence and no geometry-identity evidence rows. The existing precision already states that the point locates Apple's campus property as a whole, that the existing building lies about 0.6 km north-west of it and that the eastern lots are the PRZ 06 expansion area; the point does not locate an expansion building, and the PRZ 06 development area is not separately delineated in any captured record.

additions.distinctness_review: Screened on 27 October 2026 against every row of sites.csv, projects.csv and evidence.csv of the current dataset verified_construction_core/2026-10-27-research-ninetyfifth (re-read from site/config.json; the pass started on ninetythird), its source-records.json and identity-mapping.json, every pending queue fragment's changes.json and holds.json, claims.tsv and all sources/*-holds.json, for PRZ, PRZ 06/PRZ-06, Prineville, Apple, Baldwin Rd/Road, Crook County and by distance from the campus point. The only Atlas records within 2 km (indeed within 5 km) are the host site Apple Prineville Data Center Campus and its single project 'existing operations' (0 m; same locator). No Atlas project, source record, identity-mapping entry or pending addition names PRZ 06 or Apple's eastern expansion; the existing project's own status summary states that the PRZ 06 eastern expansion is not part of its status, and the source fragment us-west-mountain-p1 and the eighty-fourth holds (us-or-wa-p4) both held PRZ 06 as a separate future project to be added on this site once published, which it now is (published 23 October 2026 in 2026-10-23-research-fortythird). Meta's Prineville campus (held, Vitesse LLC lots on SW Connect Way west of the Apple lots) is a different owner and is not involved. The only claims.tsv entries near the point are the published us-west-mountain-p1 claim for the existing operations and this lane's claim. No other Atlas site lies within 200 km (nearest STACK POR03 and Flexential Hillsboro Starr, about 216 km, and Sabey SDC Umatilla, 221 km).
